column2: after we insert the inline extent

all extent maps in the file range
column2: however that is not necessary because

btrfs_drop_extent_cache() for us
column2: and since at this point we have the file

column1: range locked in the inode's iotree (we are in the writeback path)
no other task can come in and read stale file extent items or find none
and therefore create either stale extent maps or an extent map that
represents a hole.
So just remove that unnecessary call to btrfs_drop_extent_cache()
doing nothing and only wasting time. This call has been around since 2008
introduced in commit c8b978188c9a (""Btrfs: Add zlib compression support"")
but even back then it seems it was not necessary
locked in the inode's iotree and the call to btrfs_drop_extents() already
used to always call btrfs_drop_extent_cache().
